component: Appliances (range/oven; refrigerator; dishwasher; microwave; washer; dryer)

source: IRC §168(e)(1); IRS Publication 946 ch. 4; Rev. Proc. 87-56

basis_note: Section 1245 floor covering; Pub 946 lists carpets used in a residential rental real estate activity as 5-year property
depends_on: Installation: removable without damage vs. permanently affixed
source: IRC §168(e)(1); IRS Publication 946 ch. 4; Treas. Reg. §1.48-1(e)(2); IRS Publication 5653

basis_note: Floating or loose-laid floor covering is commonly treated like carpet; flooring permanently bonded to the structure is a structural component
depends_on: Installation: floating / removable vs. glued or permanently affixed
source: Treas. Reg. §1.48-1(e)(2); IRS Publication 5653; Whiteco Industries v. Commissioner 65 T.C. 664 (1975)

basis_note: Floors are structural components of the building

component: Furniture and furnishings (beds; sofas; tables; TVs; linens; housewares)
basis_note: Section 1245 personal property; Pub 946 lists furniture used in a residential rental real estate activity as 5-year property
rev_proc_87_56_class: 57.0 (lodging and other service use); 00.11 office furniture is 7-year
depends_on: Use: residential rental or lodging (5-year) vs. office use under asset class 00.11 (7-year)
source: IRC §168(e)(1); IRS Publication 946 ch. 4; Rev. Proc. 87-56

component: Window treatments (blinds; shades; drapery and rods)
basis_note: Removable Section 1245 furnishings
depends_on: Installation: removable vs. integral to the window system
source: Treas. Reg. §1.48-1(c); IRS Publication 5653

basis_note: Lighting that provides general illumination of the building is a structural component; decorative or accent lighting not needed for general illumination can be Section 1245
depends_on: Function: decorative / accent vs. general building illumination
source: Treas. Reg. §1.48-1(e)(2); Hospital Corporation of America v. Commissioner 109 T.C. 21 (1997); IRS Publication 5653

basis_note: Built-in cabinetry permanently attached to the building is commonly treated as a structural component; freestanding or readily removable units can be Section 1245
depends_on: Installation and permanence: built-in vs. freestanding / removable; whether it serves the business or the building
source: Whiteco Industries v. Commissioner 65 T.C. 664 (1975); IRS Publication 5653; Treas. Reg. §1.48-1(c)

basis_note: Classification generally follows the cabinetry or fixture they are part of

source: Whiteco Industries v. Commissioner 65 T.C. 664 (1975); IRS Publication 5653

source: Rev. Proc. 87-56; Treas. Reg. §1.48-1(e)(2); IRS Publication 5653

basis_note: Office furniture, fixtures and equipment

basis_note: Information systems
source: Rev. Proc. 87-56; IRS Publication 946 Appendix B
